text.text_excerpt: Love this bar, it's a cool mix of locals and tourists that is somewhat off the beaten path in the French Quarter. We stumbled upon this gem a year ago when we were there and were happy to return. The drinks are good and strong, the bartenders are friendly and quite conversational, and the prices are cheap. What else can you ask for? This is definitely a good place to take refuge from the heat and this has become a place that we stop at everytime we are in the area.

I like this bar a lot. It's a no frills dive bar. The bar tender was good. There weren't really any tourists at least not the ones who think Bourbon Street daiquiris are amazing. The drinks are cheap. I had some whiskey cokes and they were $5. The size was the typical short glass size. The beer was served in the same size which I thought was a little small but maybe that's just me. They have a juke box.

I used to go here all the time a couple years back when I lived next door, a great neighborhood bar. I still go from time to time, but it's off my beaten track. The drinks are well made and the company is great. There was a bartender there for many years who passed away a couple years back, his name was Freak. He was Harrys Corner and the bar although very good is just not the same without him.
